cards.back: When a continuous body consists of a collection of atoms/molecules arranged periodically, we call it continuous crystalline solid. For example, a single crystal without macrocracks and defects can be considered as a continuous crystalline solid.

A continuous body is a collection of millions of thousands of atoms/molecules that are
infinitesimally close and compact.
A measure system introduces units of length and directions relative to which positions can be defined.
A rigid physical object such as the earth or any “fixed stars” related to which positions can be measured and a clock relative to which time can be measured.

The scale at which a point mass is considered as a cluster of millions of thousands of atoms beyond micron meters.
A continuous body is a substance consisting of millions of thousands of atoms/molecules that are infinitesimally close and compact.

The materials are assumed to be infinitely divisible with the application of continuum
mechanics principles, without considering their discrete structures at microscopic length scale, much smaller than the phenomenon being studied.

cards.front: Nova Methodus pro Maximis et Minimis
cards.back:
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (German) established main ideas on geometric differentiation,
independently of Isaac Newton’s method of fluxions. He published his work in late 1600s.
Isaac Newton (British) created a series of terms for a derivative, known as fluxions. It was found that he completed this in 1671, but published in 1736.

1687, Isaac Newton published his work “Principia”, which states the Newton’s laws of motion, the gravitational interaction between objects (Universal), and underlies Calculus – differential and integral forms with Leibniz.
